text: dsh-theme-studio 是面向 DSH 网页客户端的外观主题插件，在设置中注册 Theme Studio 面板，并通过 DSH theme 服务应用配色。用户可以选择多种浅色与深色主题预设、设置自定义强调色、字体和内容密度，还能关闭动画、预览效果并导入或导出主题 JSON。主题偏好保存在浏览器 localStorage；无需额外 API 密钥或外部账号。

dsh-theme-studio customizes the DSH web appearance in Settings. Pick a light or dark preset, set accent colors, fonts and content density, reduce animations, preview changes, and import or export theme JSON. Preferences use browser localStorage; no API key is needed.
我想给 DSH 换一套界面配色。
能不能分别设置浅色和深色模式的强调色？
我希望把界面字体调成等宽或衬线字体。
让 DSH 的内容显示更紧凑一些。
有没有办法减少界面动画？
I want to save and share my DSH theme settings as a JSON file.
dsh-theme-studio 的功能「主题与配色」：在 Settings 的 Theme Studio 面板选择预设，或填写浅色、深色模式的强调色；插件将配色通过主题服务应用到界面。
dsh-theme-studio 的功能「导入与导出主题」：在设置面板使用导入或导出按钮，将当前偏好保存为 JSON，或读取 JSON 并校验后应用。

dsh-theme-studio README · dsh-theme-studio：A [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that customizes the UI theme: accent presets, a custom accent color, content density, font family, an animation toggle, and raw design-token overrides.

dsh-theme-studio README · What it can and cannot change：This plugin only writes design tokens that **actually exist in dsh**, verified by reading the shipped stylesheets (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-theme/lib/client.js`). Every token it writes is listed in `src/tokens.ts` and enforced by `tests/tokens.test.mjs`.

Changes go through **`ctx.theme.overrideTokens()`** — dsh's own theme service — not direct DOM writes. See [Mechanism](#mechanism) for what that buys.

That constraint has two visible consequences:
section: What it can and cannot change

text:
dsh-theme-studio README · What it can and cannot change：- **No border-radius control.** dsh hardcodes `border-radius` per component — including `50%` circles and `corner-shape: round` — and ships no radius token. There is no faithful way to offer this, so it is not offered.
- **The animation toggle is a stylesheet, not a token.** dsh ships no motion tokens, so disabling animations injects a rule compressing transition and animation durations to `0.001ms` rather than `0s` — a zero duration can stop `transitionend` / `animationend` from firing and hang components that wait on them. The sheet is owned by this plugin's effect scope, so unloading removes it.
section: What it can and cannot change

text:
dsh-theme-studio README · Features：- **12 presets**: Ocean, Forest, Sunset, Monochrome, Nord, Dracula, Gruvbox, Solarized, Tokyo Night, Catppuccin, Rosé, Ember
- **Dark-aware presets** — a preset whose dark accent differs from its light one adapts automatically when dsh enters dark mode
- **Custom accent color**, plus a separate dark-mode accent
- **Contrast guard** — a dark-mode accent below a WCAG luminance floor is lightened in steps, and the panel reports that it was adjusted
- **Density**: Compact / Comfortable / Spacious — writes dsh's own content font
  size through `ctx.theme.setFontSize()`, so it agrees with the official
  Appearance control instead of shadowing it
- **Font family**: System / Monospace / Serif
- **Animation toggle**
- **Custom CSS** — override any `--dsw-*` or `--dsh-*` token
- **Import / export** themes as validated JSON. A theme exported by an older
  version carries a `density` field; it is ignored on import, since the font size
  is host state now
- **Live preview** rendering the real tokens, showing the accent value currently in effect

```

dsh-theme-studio README · How it works：The plugin registers a `settings.section` slot (order 47). Preferences persist in `localStorage`.

dsh-theme-studio README · Mechanism：Every theme change goes through dsh's theme service:

```ts
export const inject = ['slots', 'locale', 'theme']
…
ctx.theme.overrideTokens('dsh-theme-studio', overrides)
```

`overrideTokens` stacks a partial token layer over the active theme. The service handles the rest:

dsh-theme-studio README · Mechanism：- **Layers compose in order, last writer wins per token.** Two theme plugins can coexist without either silently clobbering the other's unrelated tokens.
- **Every value is a `{ light, dark }` pair.** A single value would go illegible on the other color scheme, so the API rejects one. `src/apply.ts` builds the pairs; `tests/apply.test.mjs` asserts the shape of every value it can emit.
- **The layer is disposable.** Unloading the plugin removes exactly its layer, restoring whatever the host had underneath — including a font size the user chose in the official Appearance row.

dsh-theme-studio README · Mechanism：The layer is keyed by source (`dsh-theme-studio`), and re-publishing replaces it wholesale, so a shrinking override set can never leave a stale token behind.

An earlier version wrote custom properties straight onto `document.body` with `style.setProperty`. That happened to work — dsh's presenter only retracts variables it wrote itself — but it bypassed the stacking order, the paired values and the dispose story, and made every reset the plugin's own responsibility.

dsh-theme-studio README · Density drives the official font-size setting：`--dsh-content-font-size` is the axis the official Appearance row owns, and an
override layer sits *on top of* the theme snapshot. Overriding that token
therefore does not change the setting — it hides it, leaving the official stepper
displaying a number the UI no longer rendered.

So Density does not use an override at all. It calls
`ctx.theme.setFontSize()`, the same entry point the official control uses, and
reads back through `getTheme().fontSize`:
section: Density drives the official font-size setting

text:
dsh-theme-studio README · Density drives the official font-size setting：- The official stepper keeps showing (and setting) the same value.
- Change the size there and the matching preset highlights here; pick 15px or
  17px and nothing is highlighted, because no preset claims those.
- `--dsh-content-font-size` never appears in this plugin's override layer. The
  custom-CSS box can still set it, because that is you asking, not the plugin
deciding.
- Reset restores the size the host had before you first changed it here.
section: Density drives the official font-size setting

text:
dsh-theme-studio README · Density drives the official font-size setting：An earlier version treated the size as this plugin's own state, which produced a
control that silently disabled the official one on install (0.5.0) and then, once
the default was made inert, one that still shadowed it whenever it was used
(0.5.1).
section: Density drives the official font-size setting

text: dsh-theme-studio README · The preview is not a mock：It renders with the same variable names the application uses, so a wrong token looks wrong in the preview too, rather than being masked by a hardcoded fallback color.
section: The preview is not a mock

text:
dsh-theme-studio README · One validator for every way preferences get in：Preferences arrive three ways — `localStorage`, an imported JSON file, and a
hand-edited version of either. All three pass through `normalizePreferences()`,
which is the only place that validates: unknown enum values fall back to the
inert default, a `density: "comfortable"` written by 0.5.0 migrates to
`"default"`, malformed colors become `null`, and non-string/non-boolean fields
drop back to defaults. `parseTheme` intentionally keeps no whitelist of its own,
so the two entry points cannot drift apart.
section: One validator for every way preferences get in
